3. On-demand GPU Pricing Increase

Effective 1 June, Nebius repriced its on-demand fleet across NVIDIA B300, B200, H200 and H100, with the H100 line up close to 29% and preemptible capacity up roughly 51%. 

An increase that reaches the newest Blackwell parts and two-generation-old Hopper silicon at the same time says supply is tight the whole way down the stack.

results.title: CoreWeave Raised Prices by 25 Percent. Its Near-Term Computing Capacity Is Still Effectively Sold Out
results.author: Georgia Fearn
highlights:
CoreWeave says its near-term AI computing capacity is effectively sold out. That announcement comes after it raised prices across its product lineup by roughly 25 percent in July.

Rival AI cloud provider Nebius said Wednesday that it could sell its entire 2027 capacity today on terms similar to its latest deals, but it is deliberately holding some back for immediate customer needs. According to the company, shorter contracts can often command even higher prices.

Customers are paying premiums for near-term computing power, new contracts are becoming more profitable, and even older generations of Nvidia GPUs—the chips used to train and run AI models—are still commanding strong prices years after newer chips arrive.

...

“Pricing is extremely strong on short term deals,” Bloomberg Intelligence analyst Vasu Kasibhotla told Inc. Wednesday. Nebius, he noted, is now citing roughly $40 million in annual contract value per megawatt of data center power for short-term capacity, “materially higher than the $10-15 million the market expected just a year ago.”

...

Nebius entered 2026 with baseline annual contract value of about $12 million per megawatt. Its second-quarter deals averaged more than $20 million. It now sees an opportunity to charge $40 million to $50 million per megawatt for three-to-six-month deals.

results.title: OVHcloud chief issues customer price warning amid surging hardware costs | IT Pro
results.author: Nicole Kobie
highlights:
OVHcloud CEO Octave Klaba has urged customers to brace themselves for potential price hikes as cloud providers continue battling surging hardware costs.

In a social media post on 10 August, Klaba noted that the "significant impact" of RAM and storage costs could mean cloud prices rise by as much as 87%.

Klaba has previously warned that price rises were incoming due to rising component costs, but at the time estimated cost increases in the range of 5-10%.

...

Klaba said OVHcloud was struggling to limit unit price increases, noting that the company's prices were shifting from three times cheaper than rivals to just two times.

"In July and August, we received the latest details on RAM and disk prices for T3/Q3 2026, which now allows us to finalize the price impacts for new Public Cloud and bare metal orders, as well as for a recent portion of equipment already in production based on the latest generation of DDR5 RAM," Klaba said.

"The exercise remains a tightrope walk: we need to place the right volume of orders, month by month, over 12 months, with no guarantee on purchase prices and no way of knowing what our customers' real demand will be," he added in the translated post.

The price rises will start on new orders from the beginning of September, and equipment already in production from October.

Older generation systems, dating to 2024, will see smaller or no increases. Equipment from this year, meanwhile, will see an 87% price increase for the Game setup, 49% for "Advance" users, 40% for "Scale" users, and up to 59% for those under "High Grade" plans.

"That's +28 % on average for Gen 2024, and +51 % for Gen 2026," Klaba noted.

For public cloud, prices won't be changing directly, though there will be alterations to how companies are billed, which could boost costs by up to 22%, Klaba said.

The CEO added that he expected RAM and storage prices to continue to drive up cloud prices in 2027 and 2028, with a "return to normal hoped for in 2029."

results.title: AI Cloud Prices Rise by 25%, Intensifying Platform Competition | WEEX Crypto News
highlights:
The price increase is not a uniform trend across all GPU resources. According to the analysis reported by O'Daily, CoreWeave's GPU computing SKU prices rose by about 25% in July, while Nebius's prices for older generation GPUs increased by over 30% compared to the first quarter. The price for short-term emergency capacity was reported to be between $40 million and $50 million per MW (approximately 5.67 billion to 7.09 billion KRW).

The price reevaluation is first appearing in high-value resources that can be deployed immediately, such as short-term capacity, new generation GPUs, large clusters, and production AI inference. In contrast, existing computing resources that are lower in priority or locked in at long-term fixed prices find it difficult to reflect the same level of price increase.

results.title: The H100 Is Three Years Old and Its Rent Just Went Up 60 Percent
results.author: Neel Khokhani, Epochal
highlights:
In January, a one-year contract on an H100 cleared at somewhere between $1.50 and $2.05 per GPU hour. In July, it cleared between $2.40 and $3.20. At the midpoint, that is a rise of roughly 58 percent in six months.

...

Instead, the on-demand market for H100 capacity has been sold out in five of the last six months. The tenants holding nodes are refusing to release them back into the pool, and are paying above $2.70 an hour to keep them.

...

The move was broad. Not one SKU in one market. Between January and July, contract pricing rose across every generation of accelerator being rented, including those meant to be on their way out.

Hopper led it. H100 one month rates moved from a $1.75 to $2.10 band to $2.90 to $3.30. H200 was stronger still: one year contracts went from roughly $2.03 at the midpoint to $3.45, an increase of about 70 percent. H200 on demand capacity has been sold out for six consecutive months, with existing tenants paying above $2.90 to hold what they have.

Blackwell moved in the same direction from a higher base. B200 three year contracts rose about 42 percent at the midpoint. B300 two year contracts rose about 39 percent. GB300 three year contracts went from roughly $3.58 to $5.00, and the five year from $3.10 to $4.60, a rise of 48 percent on the longest tenor quoted. B200, B300 and H200 on demand have each been marked sold out every month since February.

AMD, which is usually the release valve when Nvidia capacity is out of reach. This time it moved too. MI300 on-demand went from a $1.50 to $2.00 band in November to $2.50 to $2.70 in July. MI325 one-year contracts rose 63 percent over the same window. The substitution route is repricing as fast as the thing being substituted for. Of all, it is the strongest. In April, a five-year VR NVL72 contract indicated at $5.00 to $5.50. In July, it indicated at $7.50 to $8.00. That is a 48 percent increase in three months on hardware that is still ramping into volume shipment. A five-year commitment on Rubin now prices roughly 65 percent above a five-year commitment on GB300.

...

The residual value of an old asset is not primarily a function of the old The residual value of an old asset is not set by its condition. It is set by the new asset’s delivery date.ays it explicitly. The December 2026 forecast for H100 rental pricing was revised up 7.4 percent to $2.85 an hour in the space of under three weeks. More interestingly, the 2028 and 2029 forecasts were also revised up, and for reasons that have nothing to do with H100 demand.

results.title: AI: The AI Compute Crunch at Ground Level (part 3). AI-RTZ #1178
results.author: Michael Parekh
highlights:
Evan Morikawa of robotics AI startup Generalist canvassed some 17 AI cloud providers for compute this year. Last winter, providers were offering reasonable prices on contracts as short as one year. By May and June, prices had jumped, contract terms had stretched to 3 to 5 years, and clusters of the latest chips carried 12 to 18 month waits. “It’s like VC currency right now to know the current price of GPUs,” he told The Information. And: “Now 1-year contracts are almost impossible to get.”

...

The number that matters most: the hourly rental price of an Nvidia H100 on a 1-year contract rose 50% from $1.73 in mid-December to $2.60 in mid-June, per Semianalysis. The H100 is a 2022 chip, TWO generations behind Nvidia’s latest. For on-demand H100s, Semianalysis often cannot quote a price at all in recent months. The column just reads ‘sold out’. 

Even at the largest cloud vendors like Amazon AWS.

results.title: 輝達 H100 GPU 租賃成本飆升 40%，AI 需求超越供給 | Gate 新聞
results.author: Gate AI 视野
highlights:
2026-08-16 20:44:19

- 輝達 H100 GPU 的租用成本從 2025 年 10 月到 2026 年 3 月飆升 40%，每 GPU 小時的價格從 $1.70 上漲至 $2.35。
- 各家雲端供應商的隨選 H100 容量實際上已售罄，叢集採購的等待時間長達 12 至 18 個月。
- 隨著次世代 B200 和 GB200 的交貨時間延長至 2026 年年中，GPU 供應商已以舊費率將合約鎖定至 2028 年。

輝達 H100 GPU 租賃成本在 2025 年 10 月至 2026 年 3 月期間上升約 40%，平均費率從每 GPU 小時 1.70 美元攀升至每 GPU 小時 2.35 美元，據 SemiAnalysis 資料顯示。價格飆升源於推論工作負載與多代理 AI 系統將運算需求推高至現有供應能力之上，導致各雲端服務商的隨選 H100 供應幾乎售罄。這代表與 2025 年的趨勢大幅反轉；當時 Neocloud 專業雲端服務商與超大規模雲端服務商擴大容量，使 GPU 租賃價格較 2023 至 2024 年的高峰下跌超過 60%。

## H100 租賃價格在供應售罄下跳升 40%

Neocloud 與超大規模雲端服務商的隨選 H100 容量幾乎售罄。如今，即使是小至 8 個節點或 64 顆 GPU 的叢集，也越來越難在短時間內取得。目前取得 H100 叢集的等候時間已達 12 至 18 個月。

更廣泛的隨選 H100 租賃市場價格介於每 GPU 小時 2.19 美元至超過 4 美元之間，取決於服務商，以及容量是提前預留還是以現貨方式購買。

## 2026 年 2 月創下單月 15% 至 20% 的價格飆升

2026 年 2 月的價格走勢尤其激進，服務商因應新的需求現實進行調整，單月錄得 15% 至 20% 的漲幅。這次單月加速大幅促成了 2025 年 10 月至 2026 年 3 月期間觀察到的整體 40% 漲幅。

## Blackwell B200 與 GB200 的交付週期延長至 2026 年年中

B200 與 GB200 部署的交付週期已延長至 2026 年年中，2026 年大部分可用容量也已分配完畢。次世代晶片的交付時間延長，進一步加劇了現有 H100 供應的壓力。

## GPU 服務商簽訂多年度合約至 2028 年

部分營運商已以舊有費率鎖定現有的 H100 合約，續約時採用先前議定的價格。少數營運商更將合約承諾延長至 2028 年。就在 18 個月前，雲端 GPU 市場幾乎還聞所未聞有長達四年的合約期限。

以優惠條件與輝達取得長期供應協議的公司，如今受益於批發採購成本與零售租賃費率之間的價差。更高的利用率與上漲的價格，轉化為 GPU 雲端服務商每個機櫃更高的營收。

results.title: We asked ~50 GPU providers for B300 pricing. Here's the map | TheAI Blog
results.author: Viacheslav Zhvart
highlights:
## Methodology, briefly

Same ask to everyone: whole nodes of 8× NVIDIA B300 SXM, terms from on-demand to 12 months, US or EU deployment. We collected public pricing pages where they exist, direct quotes where they don't, and marketplace listings where capacity trades openly. Public numbers below are as of July 23, 2026 — this market moves, so treat every figure as a dated snapshot, not gospel. Private quotes are aggregated and anonymized; we don't publish other people's confidential numbers, only the shape they form together.

## The visible market: public on-demand

Only a handful of providers publish an on-demand B300 price at all. As of the snapshot:

| Provider | On-demand, $/GPU·hr |
| --- | --- |
| Hyperstack | $7.40 |
| Verda | $7.50 |
| Nebius | $7.85 |
| AWS (Capacity Blocks) | $14.04 |

Independent price trackers put the market median around $7.85/GPU·hr — up roughly 57% since November. The floor across trackers has hovered in the $6.94–7.39 range for months. That's the market you can see with a browser.

It is worth pausing on the AWS number: a Capacity Block at $14.04 is roughly double the neocloud rate for the same silicon. That premium buys ecosystem integration, not faster matrix multiplies.

...

Everyone has heard that B300s trade "below $5". It's true — and almost none of it is rental.

Every quote we received under $5.50/GPU·hr came with the same structure: a 2-to-5-year commitment and a 20–40% down payment, wired up front. At that point you're not renting a GPU; you're taking out a mortgage on one, with the residual-value risk quietly transferred to you. Given how fast this hardware generation cycle runs — look up what an H100 rents for today versus its 2023 sticker — a five-year lock on any accelerator is a serious bet: make it with your eyes open.

...

CoreWeave and Lambda both quote B300 reserved capacity via sales only: no public price, no self-serve, and volume minimums that start conversations well above a node or two. The typical enterprise route we observed runs 2–4 weeks from first inquiry to a quote in hand.

...

The subtlest finding, and the one price tables never show: a published on-demand price is not the same thing as an available GPU.

A meaningful share of "on-demand B300" listings today lead to a queue, a "request access" form, or quiet regional stockouts. The price is real; the GPU isn't. You can be looking at a $7+ rate and be unable to deploy at any price — expensive and out of stock at the same time. When you evaluate a provider, the question isn't "what's the number on the page" but "what happens when I click launch."

...

For genuinely available on-demand capacity: public rates cluster at $6.94–7.85/GPU·hr. Reserved rates depend on the term and the prepayment; our current ones are on the rate card.

results.title: OVH Cloud warns of 87% price hikes to help it cover RAMpocalypse costs — WPS
highlights:
Octave Klaba, the CEO of France-based cloud operator OVH has warned that it will soon hike the price of server rental by up to 87 percent.

Klaba said the price OVH pays for memory rose 6x in the year to June 2026, will rise to 9x by September, and hit 12x next year. He has also seen a 7x price increase for NVMe drives, hard disk prices rise 3.5x, and the cost of CPUs, motherboards, and network cards rise by 15 to 20 percent. He thinks those prices will climb further in the near future, and blames the hyperscale buying frenzy sparked by the AI boom for the increases.

Writing on X, Klaba said OVH recently received quotes for RAM and disk prices, and argued the company must pass on its increased costs by hiking the prices for new servers as it brings them online.

The biggest rise will come to those who rent 2026-edition gaming servers, whose bills will jump by 87 percent. The cost of other recent servers will increase by 40 to 59 percent. The increases kick in from September.

The Euro-cloud will also increase the price it charges to access its 2024-era equipment when customers renew contracts, but by less than the increase charged to use new machines.

“A customer already equipped will therefore see an increase 3 to 6 times lower than for a new order,” reads a machine translation of Klaba’s Xeets.

...

Another change will see the company drop its one-month, six-month, and 24-month saving plans that lock in prices for the duration of a contract. 12 and 36 month saving plans remain.

Klaba promised to post full details later this week, and apologized for needing to make the changes.

...

“We don't know the price level of RAM and drives in 2027 yet, but the probability that prices will continue to rise is very high,” he added, before teasing us all with the prospect of eventual relief.

“We believe that this situation will last until 2028, with a return to normal hoped for in 2029,” he wrote.
